speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you've had recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis, along with fatigue, flank pain, and fever. When did these new symptoms start in relation to finishing your antibiotics, and have you noticed any changes in your urination?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Leukocyturia Present, Bacterial_Culture Negative, Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel’s_Solution 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm; Complete_Blood_Count: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; the progression from amoxicillin to cephalexin due to a rash suggests a potential drug reaction or resistant organism. Have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, or chills accompanying your flank pain and fever?

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture
REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Culture: NORMAL READINGS; Urine_Culture: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the negative cultures are surprising given the fever and flank pain. Did the rash you developed on amoxicillin return after you switched to cephalexin, or did it stay away the entire time? Also, have you experienced any nausea or vomiting with these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine
REQUEST TEST: Urine_Microscopy
Since you have no dysuria and cultures are negative, did you develop any new skin rash or joint pain alongside the fever, which might suggest a drug-induced interstitial nephritis?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum_Creatinine: Elevated; Urine_Microscopy: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to Cephalexin hypersensitivity.
Given the elevated creatinine, microscopic hematuria with eosinophils, and the timeline of symptoms following antibiotic exposure, I will stop all non-essential medications immediately. Do you have any other new rashes or joint pain since starting the cephalexin?
